title: Endomorphism span of symmetric ample lines
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $A/k$ an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety]. Call an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module] $L$ on $A$ symmetric if $[-1]^*L\simeq L$, with tensor inverse image [def-pc-module-pullback]. If $L$ and $M$ are symmetric ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] invertible modules on $A$, then there are integers $a\geq1$ and $r\geq1$ and endomorphisms $b_1,\ldots,b_r\in\operatorname{End}_k(A)$ such that $M^{\otimes a}\simeq\bigotimes_{j=1}^r b_j^*L$.

source.place: Proposition XI 1.14, p.170 (symmetric ample endomorphism-span statement).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-polarization-calculus-over-field] to $A,L$ and put $\lambda=\phi_L$, $E=\operatorname{End}^0_k(A)$, $u=\lambda^{-1}\phi_M$, and $v^\dagger=\lambda^{-1}v^\vee\lambda$. Both $L$ and $M$ are ample, so [lem-sfb-ample-polarization-positive-spectrum] gives $u^\dagger=u$ and the finite-dimensional commutative algebra $C=\mathbf Q[u]$, together with $C\otimes\mathbf R\simeq\mathbf R^d$ in which $u$ has strictly positive coordinates.

source.place: Agent assembly of the polarization and sum-of-squares inputs; see report.md for source audit and auxiliary arguments.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-split-real-algebra-positive-squares] to that algebra and $x=u$, obtaining $r\geq1$ and $q_j\in C$ with $u=\sum_jq_j^2$. The involution from [lem-sfb-polarization-calculus-over-field] fixes every $q_j$: write $q_j=\sum_i a_i u^i$ with $a_i\in\mathbf Q$ and use $u^\dagger=u$ and rational linearity. Hence $u=\sum_j q_j^\dagger q_j$.

source.place: Agent assembly of the polarization and sum-of-squares inputs; see report.md for source audit and auxiliary arguments.

proof.text: Choose a positive integer $D$ clearing the denominators of all $q_j\in\operatorname{End}_k(A)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Explicitly each is a finite sum $h\otimes(a/b)$; take a common positive multiple of the finitely many denominators $b$ and combine the resulting integer multiples of $h$. This gives actual $k$-endomorphisms $b_j$ whose rational images equal $Dq_j$. Therefore $\sum_jb_j^\dagger b_j=D^2u$.

source.place: Agent assembly of the polarization and sum-of-squares inputs; see report.md for source audit and auxiliary arguments.

proof.text:
Put $N=M^{\otimes D^2}\otimes(\bigotimes_jb_j^*L)^{-1}$. It is symmetric: $b_j\circ[-1]=[-1]\circ b_j$, so the pullback composition identities [def-pc-module-pullback] and symmetry of $L,M$ give symmetry of every factor. Pullback along $[-1]$ commutes with tensor products [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor], hence with tensor inverses of invertible modules (as $[-1]^*\mathcal O_A\cong\mathcal O_A$ by the tensor-formula definition), so $N$ is symmetric. Additivity and the pullback formula of [lem-sfb-polarization-calculus-over-field] give, in rational homomorphisms,
$$\phi_N=D^2\phi_M-\sum_j b_j^\vee\lambda b_j=\lambda(D^2u-\sum_jb_j^\dagger b_j)=0.$$
Its symmetric-kernel assertion gives $N^{\otimes2}\simeq\mathcal O_A$. Cancel the dual factors to obtain $M^{\otimes2D^2}\simeq\bigotimes_j(b_j^*L)^{\otimes2}$. Repeat each $b_j$ twice, giving $a=2D^2\geq1$ and $2r\geq1$ endomorphisms as required.
